questions.q: Where should an API key live when you call a hosted LLM from Python?
options: Hard-coded in the notebook so it is easy to find
In an environment variable read at run time
In the prompt so the model can see it
Committed to the repository next to the code
questions.explain: Keys belong in the environment (or a secrets service), never in code or version control. The official clients even read their standard variable automatically.

questions.q: In the Azure OpenAI examples, what does the model argument refer to?
options: The name of the underlying base model only
The name of your Azure subscription
The deployment name you chose when you deployed a model in your resource
The Python package version
questions.explain: Azure OpenAI calls reference your deployment name, which may or may not match the underlying model name.

questions.q: Which of these is required by the Anthropic Messages API call shown in this lesson but not by the OpenAI Responses example?
options: A max_tokens limit
A model name
An API key
Any input text
questions.explain: The Messages API requires model, max_tokens, and messages. The reply text is read from the first content block.

questions.q: Why does the lesson wrap the provider call in one small call_llm function?
options: Because the SDKs refuse to run outside a function
To hide the prompt from the model
Because retries are impossible without it
So the provider can be swapped, and a fake used in tests, without changing the rest of the pipeline
questions.explain: All three calls have the same basic shape, so one narrow function isolates the provider-specific details and makes offline testing easy.

questions.q: The lesson tested its retry loop with a fake model. What did that show?
options: That real APIs never fail
That the loop retries transient errors with backoff and eventually returns an answer, with no API access needed
That the fake model is more accurate than a real one
That retries should never be used
questions.explain: The fake failed twice then answered, so you could verify retry behavior offline. The official SDKs may also retry by default, so check their current docs.
